ALGER, 21/06/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Algér: ALGIERS, 06/21/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Algérie Poste has announced a major modernization of its automated teller machines (ATMs) with a new PIN verification protocol. Starting today, customers will be required to enter their secret code on the second interface after inserting their card, thereby reducing transaction times.
Modernisation des GAB : Algérie Poste re: ATM Modernization: Algérie Poste enhances the efficiency of electronic banking services
L’opérateur public Algérie Poste (AP) a: The public operator Algérie Poste (AP) announced this Sunday, June 21, 2026, the entry into force of a major update to its automated teller machines (ATMs) nationwide. From now on, customers will have to verify their PIN (personal identification number) on the second screen interface, after inserting their bank card, instead of the first one as was previously practiced. This innovation, being progressively deployed across the network's 3,200 ATMs, aims to optimize transaction duration while improving the efficiency and fluidity of electronic banking services.
Selon les premières estimations, cette m: According to initial estimates, this modification is expected to reduce users' waiting times during withdrawals or balance inquiries by an average of 25%. "This change is part of our ongoing effort to improve service quality and customer satisfaction," stated an official from Algérie Poste's information systems department. Real-world tests, particularly in the wilayas of Algiers, Oran, and Constantine, confirmed a significant drop in queues during peak hours.
Cette modernisation des GAB s’inscrit da: This ATM modernization takes place in a context where electronic banking services occupy a central place in the digitalization strategy of the Algerian economy. With over 30 million mobile internet subscribers and a mobile penetration rate exceeding 120% in 2025, according to data from ARPCE (Autorité de Régulation de la Poste et des Communications Électroniques), citizens' expectations regarding transaction speed and security are constantly increasing. The ATM update directly addresses this demand while reducing fraud risks associated with the premature display of the PIN code on the main screen.
Sur le plan économique, cette innovation: Economically, this innovation could also contribute to better financial inclusion, particularly in remote wilayas where access to traditional banking services remains limited. Algérie Poste, which manages a network of 4,500 contact points (ATMs, postal agencies, and post offices) spread across the 58 wilayas, plays a key role in the democratization of financial services. Reducing waiting times could thus encourage more citizens to adopt electronic payment methods, in line with the objectives of the Digital Plan 2030.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
Le secteur des technologies de l’informa: The Information and Communication Technology (ICT) sector in Algeria is experiencing sustained growth, driven by massive investments in infrastructure and digital services. In 2025, the mobile penetration rate reached 125%, with more than 60 million active lines, according to the latest statistics from ARPCE. At the same time, the number of fixed and mobile internet subscribers exceeds 32 million, with an annual growth rate of 8% for mobile broadband (4G/5G).
Dans ce cadre, Algérie Télécom, opérateu: In this context, historical operator Algérie Télécom has invested more than 150 billion Algerian dinars since 2020 to modernize its network, notably through the deployment of 5G in major wilayas. ARPCE, the independent regulatory authority, oversees these developments while ensuring compliance with quality and security standards. Private operators such as Mobilis (a subsidiary of Algérie Télécom), Djezzy, and Ooredoo complete this ecosystem by offering innovative services, such as digital wallets and mobile payment solutions, which are seeing growing adoption.
The Director General of Algérie Poste, Mr. Mohamed El Hachemi, welcomed this technological breakthrough during a press conference held in Algiers. "This update is the result of several months of work with our technical partners and internal teams. It illustrates our commitment to offering increasingly efficient and secure services to our fellow citizens," he stated. He also recalled that this innovation adds to other services offered by Algérie Poste, such as bill payment, money transfer, and online bank account opening.
De son côté, le président de l’APW (Asse: For his part, the president of the APW (Popular Assembly of Wilaya) of Algiers, Mr. Abdelkader Zoukh, highlighted the positive impact of this modernization on citizens. "In a wilaya as dense as Algiers, where queues at ATMs can be long, this improvement will be greatly appreciated. It is part of the public service modernization dynamic that we have been pursuing for several years," he indicated.
Algerie Poste prévoit de généraliser cet: Algérie Poste plans to roll out this update to all its ATMs by the end of July 2026. An awareness campaign will be launched across all 58 wilayas to inform users of the new protocols and the benefits of this innovation. In addition, training sessions will be organized for contact point agents to ensure optimal customer support.
À plus long terme, l’opérateur envisage: In the longer term, the operator plans to integrate biometric technologies, such as facial recognition or fingerprint authentication, to enhance transaction security. These solutions, already tested in certain pilot wilayas, could be deployed by 2027, in collaboration with the competent authorities and sector stakeholders.
